claim: Most portable computers have no keyboards.
originalWording: Most portable computers have no keyboards.

sources.title: How My Predictions Are Faring — Ray Kurzweil
sources.locator: The Computer Itself, prediction 7, printed p. 16

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source and full record for attribution limits.

reference.criterion: Across newly sold portable computing devices, including smartphones and tablets, most lack physical keyboards.
reference.rationale: Touchscreen portables were real by 2009, but widespread keyboard-equipped phones and notebooks make full majority fulfillment unpersuasive then. By the mid-2010s, touch-first smartphones dominated portable computing unit volumes. Gartner’s 2013 smartphone/platform mix supports the transition; the exact crossover is not established.

evidence.title: iPhone App Store downloads top 10 million
evidence.note: Multi-Touch feature paragraph and cellular/Wi-Fi application-delivery paragraphs. This documents touch-based software use on the supported devices. Evidence limits: It does not quantify the share of keyboard-free portable computers; the added original iPhone announcement directly describes a soft keyboard.

evidence.title: Pew: Americans and their gadgets
evidence.note: US survey, seven broad device categories; median three categories. A proxy for device ownership, not a direct census of worn processors or 2009 body networks.. US survey, seven broad device categories; median three categories. A proxy for device ownership, not a direct census of worn processors or 2009 body networks.

evidence.title: Gartner: Worldwide smartphone sales in 2013
evidence.note: 968 million smartphones; Android plus iOS dominated. Inferring physical-keyboard-free portable computing requires a population definition, not simply counting all feature phones.. 968 million smartphones; Android plus iOS dominated. Inferring physical-keyboard-free portable computing requires a population definition, not simply counting all feature phones.

evidence.title: Apple reinvents the phone with iPhone
evidence.note: iPhone is a Revolutionary Mobile Phone section: SMS and touch-keyboard paragraph. The original iPhone announcement explicitly describes an onscreen keyboard, directly supporting the availability of physical-keyboard-free portables. Evidence limits: The announcement is not a device-population share study and does not establish majority adoption in 2009.

strict.criterion: Conventional notebook/laptop computers mostly lose their physical keyboards.
strict.rationale: That narrower population does not fulfill the prediction. It is a population sensitivity, not the only legitimate meaning of portable computer.
